fixed_global_transition_model.name: UNORDERED_FIXED_POINT_LOGIC_WITH_COUNTING_GLOBAL_DECISION
fixed_global_transition_model.semantics: The exact decision/progress invariant is required to be definable uniformly in fixed-point logic with counting over the unordered relational encoding of the constraint instance, without an externally supplied linear order or rank operator.
fixed_global_transition_model.why_global: FPC permits global inflationary/fixed-point iteration and counting and is strictly richer than bounded-local Datalog; this route is therefore not merely R44AE under a new name.

published_theorem.title: Affine systems of equations and counting infinitary logic
published_theorem.statement_used: Testing solvability of systems of equations over a fixed finite Abelian group is not definable in the infinitary logic with finitely many variables and counting; consequently it is not definable in least fixed-point logic or its extension with counting (FPC/IFPC) on the unordered relational encodings considered.
published_theorem.tractability_fact: The same affine CSP is polynomial-time decidable by finite-group/linear-algebraic methods; over GF(2), Gaussian elimination is an exact polynomial-time solver.

derived_TRUMP_barrier.claim: A TRUMP universal exact transition/decision semantics exhausted by unordered FPC+counting cannot be complete even for the affine/GF(2) tractable subclass already represented in TRUMP.
reason: Affine solvability is a special exact CSP/constraint family solvable in polynomial time.
The cited theorem shows that this solvability property is not definable in the fixed unordered FPC/counting language.

Therefore an FPC-only universal decision invariant would fail L1/L2 already on a tractable affine subclass; adding more fixed-point iterations inside the same language does not repair the expressiveness gap.
TRUMP's existing exact GF(2) route therefore genuinely uses algebraic/rank information not captured by this fixed FPC model.

important_scope_boundary.reason: On ordered finite structures, classical fixed-point logics have much greater expressive power (Immerman-Vardi phenomena). The cited inexpressibility result must not be transferred to an ordered/canonically ordered algorithmic model without a separate theorem.

dead_zone_mapping.meaning: A global observer can still have an information dead zone if its invariant language cannot represent rank/affine solvability.

what_is_not_proved: No lower bound is claimed for algorithms that use the concrete input order/variable indices as computational data.
No lower bound is claimed for fixed-point logics extended with suitable rank/linear-algebra operators.
No runtime lower bound is claimed for arbitrary polynomial-time algorithms.
This result does not prove P!=NP.

TRUMP_architecture_consequence.rule: A future global implicit invariant language must at minimum preserve the exact algebraic power already needed for GF(2)/affine routes; replacing explicit state by a weaker symmetric fixed-point/counting language is not semantics-preserving.

next_admissible_math.question: Can one fix a global implicit language with explicit linear-algebra/rank operators (or another exact algebraic primitive), prove polynomial evaluation/update cost, and then either prove universal 3CNF totality or establish a theorem barrier for that precisely stronger language?
forbidden: assuming variable labels give canonical semantic order without accounting for representation invariance
dropping the affine/GF2 route while claiming universal exactness
